scenario: [LIMP.13.3]: two programs share a schema by its own name when each imports one library under one path. `pub` and `hub` both import `lib`'s `Ref`, and `pub` publishes one. `hub` receives the record through its own `assert_external`, under the own name `lib.Ref` and that name's `schema_hash` ([RFCS.23.3]). `pub` holds its Trig alone, since a `publish` asserts nothing there ([LTIE.4.3]): 1 fact; `hub` holds 1. A receiver that looked the record up by any other name refuses it, and `forward_external` fails the fixture on a refusal ([RCTS.1.2.29]). PATH PINNED: libds's `ds_engine_assert_external` (through pyds `Engine.assert_external`, runner.py) and the Mercury runtime's `ds.fact_receive.assert_external` (test_behave.m's `receive_on_tier`).

libraries.lib:
schema Ref scope ttl 1_h:
    v: Int

pub.rules_ds:
from lib import Ref

schema Trig scope logical:
    v: Int key

rule up:
    Trig t
->
    publish Ref v: t.v
